summary: Iteration 8 backend testing: validated STATIC_ROUTES expansion (15 routes) + sitemap sync single-source-of-truth refactor. Created /app/backend/tests/test_seo_prerender_iter8.py with 92 tests covering: 15-route inventory, per-route HTML shell (title keywords, description>60 chars, canonical, absolute https og:image, JSON-LD, main#__seo_prerender+h1) for all 10 new routes, JSON-LD schema types (CollectionPage.hasPart for /brands hub, Brand+BreadcrumbList per brand page, Service+BreadcrumbList per new solution), per-brand og:image differentiation (jabra/logitech point to /brand-logos/<slug>.png, all 7 brand images unique), sitemap XML validity, presence of all 12 new URLs + 12 extra pages, no duplicate <loc>, blog post regression sync, /brands/roomz + /solutions/business-apps regression. Result: 92/92 passed. Also reran prior iter5/6/7 suites: 79/79 passed.
critical_code_review_comments: seo_prerender.py: _BRAND_PAGES lookup in /brands hub hasPart uses `_BRAND_PAGES[s]['name'] if s in _BRAND_PAGES else 'ROOMZ'` — hardcoded 'ROOMZ' fallback is fragile; if another brand slug is later added to the ecosystem list without adding it to _BRAND_PAGES it will silently mis-label. Consider moving ROOMZ into _BRAND_PAGES (or defining a single ECOSYSTEM order list) so there is one source of truth for brand display names.

seo_prerender.py file is now ~830 lines and mixes registry data with rendering logic. Approaching the 700-line threshold; consider splitting brand + solution registries into a separate module (e.g. seo_registry.py) with seo_prerender.py owning render/resolve logic only.

server.py sitemap uses a lazy import `from seo_prerender import STATIC_ROUTES` inside _build_sitemap_static_pages(). Fine functionally, but move to top-level for consistency and to surface any circular-import issues at boot rather than at first request.
